name: ANAVAH
why: Performance-focused owner-layout bluewater cat with an unusually strong recent cruising refit: 2025 standing rigging, 2024 North 3Di sails, about 1,600Ah lithium, about 2,440W solar, battery-run A/C, high-output watermaker, modern Raymarine/Starlink, CopperCoat and a proven long-range platform. Broker supplied a Dec. 2024 pre-purchase survey and says the major survey deficiencies were subsequently addressed.
risks: Known lightning-strike history remains the primary diligence issue. The Dec. 2024 survey documented cracked standing-rigging fittings, water in port saildrive oil, engine cooling/pressure issues, DIY electrical concerns, nonworking heads/plumbing and a decommissioned watermaker. Broker says significant deficiencies were later fixed, including new standing rigging, engine/saildrive service, new toilets/plumbing and CopperCoat, but now says the supporting repair invoices are normally released only after an in-person showing and as a buyer moves toward an offer. The repair bridge and lightning-claim file therefore remain unverified, and current engine hours still need confirmation.
stage: Repair records gated behind in-person showing — Max decision
next_step: YOUR DECISION: either schedule an in-person St Augustine showing to unlock the repair invoices/pre-offer diligence, or put ANAVAH on hold because the broker will not provide the repair bridge first. Sellers are open to reasonable offers, but no travel, offer or location disclosure should be sent automatically.
listed_date_notes: No defensible first-listing date established in the Sep. 4 email-reconciliation pass.
notes: ANAVAH is hauled out in yard storage in St Augustine and available for showings by appointment. Andrew says professionals addressed the major survey findings, believes the updates should improve a new survey, and indicates some price flexibility, but the documentation is intentionally gated until a showing/pre-offer stage. Treat repair claims as unverified until records or independent current survey evidence corroborate them.

name: THE LIGHT
why: The equipment list initially looked compelling for offshore use: major 2019–20 rig/crossbeam work, newer sails, CopperCoat, serviced saildrives, relatively moderate engine hours and upgraded lithium/solar/Victron systems.
risks: Broker has now explicitly disclosed that this is a hurricane-damaged boat. That materially changes the investment thesis and likely explains the 2020 mast, boom, standing-rigging and forward-crossbeam replacements. The loss event, structural damage scope, insurance file, repair engineering, yard invoices, pre/post-repair surveys, moisture/core findings and resale/insurability implications are not yet documented. Generator and A/C were also removed.
refit_display: Unknown until hurricane repair file is reviewed
all_in_display: Do not underwrite at ask until casualty/repair documentation is reviewed
stage: Hurricane damage disclosed — Max decision gate
next_step: YOUR DECISION: decide whether a hurricane-rebuild boat remains in scope. If yes, take Brent's requested call only to unlock the full casualty/insurance/repair file and require engineering scope, repair invoices, pre/post surveys and current moisture/structural evidence before any travel or offer. No automatic reply or call initiated.
listed_date_notes: No defensible first-listing date established in the Sep. 4 email-reconciliation pass.
notes: Material negative disclosure received Sep. 4. Keep visible as a cautionary comp rather than treating the 2019–20 replacement work as a pure-value refit.

name: MAC LERIC
ask_display: €400,000 (EU VAT paid; seller indicates reasonable flexibility)
why: Exceptionally detailed maintenance/refit provenance for a 2009 cruising cat: complete 2025 Z-Spars mast and standing rigging, 2024 Incidences mainsail plus unused replacement genoa, about 2,300W solar, Victron inverter/charging, 9.5kVA Onan, Aquabase 105 L/h watermaker, dual A/C and private-use history. The seller-side broker supplied a forensic document register, supporting-document package and major-maintenance history rather than relying only on listing claims.
risks: Twin Volvo D2-55s are around 4,700 hours and no major overhaul/rebuild has yet been established. MS130 saildrive diaphragm replacement date cannot be substantiated since at least 2017 and neither drive has had a significant overhaul during current ownership. Generator has seen little/no use since Apr. 2024; house bank is 720Ah AGM rather than lithium; lithium readiness is unproven; A/C seawater pump is currently absent; watermaker has no documented major service/membrane date; and there is no recent comprehensive condition/moisture survey. Original mast was replaced after damage developed at its foot, although seller reports no related bulkhead/chainplate structural repair.
stage: Mechanical questions forwarded to seller-side broker — waiting
next_step: Wait for Chris and the French-side broker to return vessel-specific evidence of major 4,000-hour engine service, top-end/injector/heat-exchanger work, compression testing, oil analysis or overhaul/rebuild, plus any remaining answers. Chris's comments about older Volvo longevity are broker opinion, not MAC LERIC evidence, so do not reduce the mechanical reserve until records land. No reply, call, offer or travel is needed now.
listed_date_notes: No defensible first-listing date established in the Sep. 4 email-reconciliation pass.
notes: Seller reports no grounding, collision, storm damage, insurance claim, osmosis, wet core/delamination or persistent leaks to his knowledge. Historic steering-sector support repair was explained as damage from someone stepping on a non-load-bearing support. Loaded cruising estimate is about 14–15 tonnes. Seller says there is room for a reasonable price discussion on a straightforward timely sale. Chris agreed that the engine-history question is the right diligence item and is forwarding it to the seller-side broker.
